speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a psychiatric condition and new onset movement disorder; can you tell me what specific movements you are experiencing and when they started?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is helpful context; given the onset of these movements two months after starting risperidone, are the movements rhythmic and repetitive, such as lip-smacking or tongue protrusion?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Inability to remain still, persistent feeling of restlessness. I also have Frequent fidgeting, Repetitive crossing and uncrossing of legs, Pacing.

speaker: Doctor
text: The symptoms you describe—fidgeting, leg crossing/uncrossing, and an inability to remain still—are characteristic of akathisia, a common side effect of antipsychotics like risperidone. Is this inner restlessness making it difficult for you to sit or stay in one place for long periods?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Recently diagnosed with schizophrenia. No other significant past medical history. Social history: College student, lives with parents. Denies tobacco, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Akathisia (secondary to risperidone use in schizophrenia).

The clinical picture of new-onset inner restlessness, fidgeting, and leg crossing/uncrossing appearing two months after starting risperidone is highly specific for akathisia. No further tests or questions are required to confirm this diagnosis or initiate management with a beta-blocker or dose adjustment.
